title: Rain and Snow
subtitle: Four seasons in Chicago, and what you wear for each one.
description: An A1 reading and listening text about weather and clothes through the year in a cold American city.
source: authored for this site; no source document
passage: Chicago has four seasons, and they are all very different.
Winter is long and cold. There is a lot of snow, and the wind from the lake is bad. I wear a big coat, a hat, and boots. Some mornings the street is white and quiet.
Spring is wet. It rains a lot, so I take an umbrella to work. The park near our apartment is green again, and the days are longer.
Summer is hot. People sit outside, the kids play in the water, and nobody wants to cook. Jack and I eat on the step in front of the building.
Fall is my favorite. It is not hot and it is not cold. The trees are red and yellow for three weeks, and then the wind takes the leaves away.
Then it is cold again. In Chicago, you always have a coat near the door.

exercises.title: Understanding the Text
exercises.instructions: Read again and choose the best answer.

items.prompt: What makes the Chicago winter hard?
options: The snow and the cold wind from the lake
items.explanation: “There is a lot of snow, and the wind from the lake is bad.”

items.prompt: Why does Emma take an umbrella in spring?
options: Because it is her favorite season
items.explanation: “Spring is wet. It rains a lot, so I take an umbrella to work.”

items.prompt: What do people do in the summer?
options: They stay outside and don't cook
items.explanation: “People sit outside… nobody wants to cook.”

items.prompt: Where do Emma and Jack eat in summer?
options: On the step in front of their building
items.explanation: “Jack and I eat on the step in front of the building.”

items.prompt: Which season does Emma like best?
How long are the trees red and yellow?
items.explanation: “The trees are red and yellow for three weeks.”
